entry: Informal group of [[Scavenger|scavenging]] birds in the family Accipitridae, found in Europe, Asia and Africa. Old World vultures are not closely related to the [[New World vulture|New World vultures]] and condors; the resemblance between the two groups results from convergent evolution. Like other vultures, they feed mostly on carcasses and find them by sight. More than half of the species are listed as vulnerable, endangered or critically endangered by the IUCN Red List. In [[Asia]], the most notable declines are due to diclofenac, an anti-inflammatory drug given to working farm animals; vultures that eat carcasses containing it suffer kidney failure and die. Populations in [[India]] and [[Pakistan]] have fallen by up to 99%. Within [[Africa]], poisoning and the vulture trade account for roughly 90% of declines. Meloxicam has been found harmless to vultures and is proposed as an acceptable alternative.

2003 South Korean action thriller film directed by Park Chan-wook. A loose adaptation of the Japanese manga *Old Boy* by Garon Tsuchiya and Nobuaki Minegishi, *Oldboy* follows Oh Dae-su, who is imprisoned for 15 years without knowing his captor's motives. After his release he seeks revenge while falling in love with a sushi chef, Mi-do. The film won the Grand Prix at the 2004 [[Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]], where [[Quentin Tarantino]] was jury president. It is the second part of Park's Vengeance Trilogy. Its success led to an unauthorized Hindi remake in 2006 and an American adaptation in 2013.

Family of [[Flowering plant|flowering plants]], mostly shrubs and trees, in the order Lamiales. Also known as the olive family, Oleaceae comprises 28 [[Genus|genera]] and around 700 species, though estimates range from 600 to 900. Notable members include [[Olive|olive]], [[Fraxinus|ash]], jasmine, lilac, privet and forsythia. The flowers are often numerous and strongly fragrant, and most fruits are dispersed by wind or animals. The family is subcosmopolitan, ranging from the subarctic to southern Africa, Australia and South America, but its major centers of diversity are in Southeast Asia and Australia. Much of the variation in species estimates comes from the genus Jasminum, which has been accepted with between 200 and 450 species. Oleaceae is an ancient family, and some of its genera may be relictual populations that persisted in isolation for long periods.

Ukrainian professional boxer. As an amateur, Usyk won heavyweight gold medals at the 2011 World Championships and 2012 Olympics. He became the first Ukrainian undisputed champion in 2018, when he won the undisputed cruiserweight title. In 2021 he defeated Anthony Joshua to win the WBA, IBF and WBO heavyweight titles. In May 2024 he defeated Tyson Fury to add the WBC title and become undisputed heavyweight champion. In July 2025 he knocked out Daniel Dubois to become a two-time undisputed heavyweight champion, a feat only [[Muhammad Ali]] had achieved before him.

Sensory system responsible for the [[Sense of smell|sense of smell]] (olfaction). Olfaction is one of the special senses, directly associated with specific organs. Most mammals and reptiles have a main olfactory system, which detects airborne substances, and an accessory system, which senses fluid-phase stimuli. In the nose, odor molecules dissolved in mucus bind to receptors on the cilia of olfactory neurons in the [[Epithelium|olfactory epithelium]]. The resulting electrical signals travel along olfactory nerve fibers through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to the olfactory bulbs. From there, information reaches the olfactory cortex, which includes the piriform cortex, amygdala and olfactory tubercle. The olfactory system and the sense of [[Taste|taste]] are often grouped as the chemosensory system, because both give the brain information about the chemical composition of objects.

Controversial form of government in which power rests with a small number of people. Leaders of oligarchies, called oligarchs, are generally characterized by titles of [[Nobility|nobility]] or high amounts of [[Wealth|wealth]]. The word comes from [[Ancient Greek|Greek]] words meaning rule by few. [[Aristotle]] used the term to mean rule by the rich and treated oligarchy as a corruption of aristocracy. In the early 20th century, Robert Michels argued in his iron law of oligarchy that even democracies tend to become oligarchic, because dividing labor creates a ruling class focused on maintaining its power. In Athens, [[Themistocles]] became archon in 493 BC and greatly increased the power of the navy, allowing the lower classes to influence politics. Business groups may be considered oligarchies if they are the largest private owners in a country, have political power and control several businesses.

Fruit of *Olea europaea*, a subtropical evergreen tree in the family [[Oleaceae]]. The olive is a [[Fruit|drupe]] similar in structure to the [[Cherry|cherry]] or [[Peach|peach]]. One of the first fruit trees to be domesticated, it was first cultivated in the Eastern Mediterranean between 6,000 and 4,000 BC and spread around the Mediterranean Basin through trade and human migration. Modern cultivars trace primarily to the Near East, the [[Aegean Sea|Aegean Sea]] and the [[Strait of Gibraltar|Strait of Gibraltar]]. Olive oil is a core ingredient in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines, and the fruit is also eaten as table olives. The olive branch is a symbol of peace. Spain, Italy and Greece lead world commercial production, and about 80% of harvested olives are processed into oil.

English military and political leader, Lord Protector (1653–58). Cromwell rose to prominence in the [[English Civil War]] as a Parliamentarian commander. He commanded the New Model Army [[Cavalry|cavalry]] under Thomas Fairfax. He was a leading advocate of the execution of Charles I in January 1649, which led to the establishment of the Commonwealth of England. He was named Lord Protector in December 1653 and held the post until his death. His son Richard succeeded him, but weakness led to a power vacuum and the 1660 Stuart Restoration. Cromwell's body was removed from [[Westminster Abbey|Westminster Abbey]] and hanged at Tyburn on 30 January 1661. His reputation is contested. Critics cite his use of military force to gain power, his role in the execution of Charles I and the brutality of the 1649 conquest of Ireland. [[Winston Churchill]] described him as a military dictator, while others regard him as a hero of liberty.

American filmmaker and author. Stone served in the [[Vietnam War|Vietnam War]] from 1967 to 1968 and was twice wounded. He began as a screenwriter with *Midnight Express* (1978), for which he won an [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for Best Adapted Screenplay. He won Academy Awards for Best Director for *Platoon* (1986), which also won Best Picture, and *Born on the Fourth of July* (1989). Other films include *JFK* (1991), *Nixon* (1995) and *Snowden* (2016). Many of his films address controversial American political issues, and critics have accused Stone of promoting conspiracy theories.

English actress known for comedic and dramatic roles. Her breakthrough came in the Channel 4 sitcom *Peep Show* (2003–2015). She won a British Academy Television Award for Best Actress for the ITV crime drama *Broadchurch* (2013–2017), and played Queen [[Elizabeth II|Elizabeth II]] in the [[Netflix|Netflix]] series *The Crown*, winning a Golden Globe Award and a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress. She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her portrayal of [[Anne, Queen of Great Britain]] in *The Favourite* (2018).

British and Australian singer and actress. With over 100 million records sold, she is one of the best-selling music artists of all time. She starred in the 1978 musical film *Grease* with [[John Travolta]]; their duet "You're the One That I Want" is one of the best-selling singles of all time. Her solo recordings include the Grammy-winning "I Honestly Love You" (1974) and "Physical" (1981). She represented the United Kingdom at the [[Eurovision Song Contest|Eurovision Song Contest]] in 1974, finishing fourth. Having had breast cancer three times, she became an advocate for [[Breast cancer|breast cancer]] research and an activist for [[Animal rights|animal rights]].

British-born American actress of Hollywood's Golden Age. She appeared in 49 films between 1935 and 1988, most often opposite [[Errol Flynn|Errol Flynn]] in adventure films such as *Captain Blood* (1935). Her performance as Melanie Hamilton in *Gone with the Wind* (1939) earned her the first of five [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations. She won Best Actress Oscars for *To Each His Own* (1946) and *The Heiress* (1949). She lived in [[Paris|Paris]] from the 1950s and was appointed Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire at the age of 101. Her younger sister was the actress Joan Fontaine.

Magnesium iron silicate mineral, (Mg,Fe)₂SiO₄. Olivine forms a solid solution series between forsterite (Mg₂SiO₄) and fayalite (Fe₂SiO₄). Forsterite melts at almost 1,900 °C (3,450 °F), while fayalite melts at about 1,200 °C (2,190 °F). It is the primary component of the Earth's upper mantle but weathers quickly at the surface. Translucent olivine is used as the gemstone [[Peridot|peridot]], and some of the finest gem-quality olivine comes from Zabargad Island in the [[Red Sea|Red Sea]]. It occurs in [[Igneous rock|igneous rocks]] such as basalt and gabbro, and rocks with more than 40% olivine are called peridotites.

Monumental [[Basalt|basalt]] sculptures of human heads made by the [[Mesoamerica|Mesoamerican]] Olmec civilization. Seventeen confirmed examples are known from four sites in the [[Olmecs|Olmec]] heartland on the Gulf Coast of Mexico, and a throne at Takalik Abaj in Guatemala may have been carved from a colossal head. They range in height from 1.17 to 3.4 m (3.8 to 11.2 ft). The boulders came from the Sierra de Los Tuxtlas, more than 150 km (93 mi) away. The largest, abandoned near the source of its stone, is estimated at 36 to 45 t (40 to 50 short tons). The heads are thought to portray powerful individual rulers, and their distinctive headdresses may be protective helmets. Most have been dated to the Early Preclassic period (1500–1000 BC). The first head was found at Tres Zapotes in 1862, and an excavation by Matthew Stirling in 1938 spurred the first archaeological investigations of Olmec culture.

Earliest known major civilization of [[Mesoamerica|Mesoamerica]], centered in what are now the Mexican states of Veracruz and Tabasco. The Olmecs flourished from about 1200 to 400 BC. They were centered first at San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán and from the 10th century BC at La Venta. By about 400 BC their major centers had been abandoned, although elements of their tradition lived on in successor societies. The Olmecs appear to have practiced ritual bloodletting and played the Mesoamerican ballgame, practices shared by nearly all later Mesoamerican societies. They are known especially for their artwork, including colossal heads. Olmec hieroglyphs dating to about 650 BC have been found on roller stamps and stone artifacts. The name Olmec derives from the Nahuatl term for [[Natural rubber|rubber]] people, a name applied in error to the ancient culture by early 20th-century archaeologists.

Nigerian head of state (1976–79; 1999–2007). A former army general, Obasanjo played a major role in combating Biafran separatists in the [[Nigerian Civil War|Nigerian Civil War]] and accepted their surrender in 1970. After the assassination of Murtala Muhammed in 1976, he became military head of state and oversaw the 1979 election, handing power to the civilian president Shehu Shagari. In 1995 he was convicted of involvement in a planned coup under Sani Abacha, despite protesting his innocence, and he was released after Abacha's death in 1998. He won the 1999 presidential election as the candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party and was re-elected in 2003. As president he de-politicized the military and privatized public enterprises. He supported the formation of the [[African Union|African Union]] and chaired it from 2004 to 2006. Supporters credit him with Nigeria's transition to democracy, while critics argue that his administrations were marked by [[Corruption|corruption]] and human rights abuses.

Series of international multi-sport events, held as separate Summer and Winter Games. The Games are open to amateur and professional athletes, and each team represents a [[Sovereign state|sovereign state]] or territory. They were inspired by the [[Ancient Olympic Games|ancient Olympic Games]] held at Olympia, Greece, from the 8th century BC to the 4th century AD. [[Pierre de Coubertin|Pierre de Coubertin]] founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894, and the first modern Games were held in [[Athens|Athens]] in 1896. The Summer and Winter Games are each held every four years, two years apart. Over 14,000 athletes competed at the 2020 Summer and 2022 Winter Games combined, in 40 sports and 448 events. The Games have been disrupted by world wars, Cold War boycotts and the COVID-19 pandemic: the 1916, 1940 and 1944 Games were canceled, and the 2020 Games were postponed to 2021.

Competitive strength sport in which athletes lift a loaded barbell from the ground to overhead. Athletes compete in two lifts: the snatch, a wide-grip lift in which the bar is raised overhead in one motion, and the clean and jerk, in which it is lifted to the shoulders and then overhead. Each lifter has three attempts at each lift, and the score is the combined total, in kilograms, of the heaviest successful lifts. A third lift, the clean and press, was contested from 1924 to 1972. Weightlifting has been held at every [[Summer Olympic Games|Summer Olympic Games]] since 1920. Because the Olympic lifts are performed quickly and require mobility, they test explosive power, unlike the limit strength tested by [[Powerlifting|powerlifting]]. The International Weightlifting Federation governs the sport and runs the World Weightlifting Championships each year.

[[Shield volcano]] in the Tharsis region of [[Mars|Mars]]. Measured by the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter, it is 21.287 km (69,840 ft) high, about 2.5 times the height of [[Mount Everest|Mount Everest]] above sea level. It is Mars's tallest volcano and tallest planetary mountain. Its summit has six nested [[Caldera|calderas]]. Olympus Mons is the youngest of the large Martian volcanoes and last erupted about 25 million years ago. Its great size is likely due to the lack of mobile tectonic plates on Mars, which lets a stationary hotspot feed the volcano.

Sacred syllable, [[Mantra|mantra]] and invocation in [[Hinduism|Hinduism]], Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism. Om is described as a sonic representation of the divine and is the basic tool for [[Meditation|meditation]] in the [[Yoga|yogic]] path to liberation. Its written form is the most important symbol in Hinduism. The syllable is often placed at the beginning and end of chapters in the [[Vedas|Vedas]] and the [[Upanishads|Upanishads]], and it is chanted before scriptural recitation, in prayer, and at rites of passage such as weddings. Om emerged in the Vedic corpus as an encapsulated form of Samavedic chants. The Aitareya Brahmana suggests that its three phonetic components, a, u and m, correspond to the three stages of cosmic creation. Other names include Pranava, meaning fore-sound, and Onkara. Its etymology has long been disputed.

Largest city in [[Nebraska|Nebraska]] and county seat of Douglas County (pop., 2020: 486,051). Omaha was founded in 1854 along the [[Missouri River|Missouri River]] and became an important transportation and railroad hub. The Omaha Stockyards, once the world's largest, made the city a meatpacking center. It hosted the Trans-Mississippi Exposition, a [[World's fair|World's Fair]], in 1898. Omaha is home to the headquarters of four Fortune 500 companies, including [[Berkshire Hathaway|Berkshire Hathaway]] and [[Union Pacific Railroad|Union Pacific]]. Its institutions include the Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium and the annual College World Series. Inventions credited to Omaha include the Reuben sandwich, cake mix and the TV dinner.

Sultanate on the southeastern tip of the [[Arabian Peninsula|Arabian Peninsula]], in West Asia. Its capital is [[Muscat|Muscat]], and Oman has an area of 315,331 sq km (121,750 sq mi) and a population of about 5.46 million. Oman is an [[Absolute monarchy|absolute monarchy]] ruled by a sultan, who is both head of state and head of government. The Al Bu Said dynasty has ruled since 1744, and in the 19th century Omani influence extended as far as [[Zanzibar|Zanzibar]]. In the 20th century Oman came under the influence of the British Empire while remaining sovereign. Sultan Qaboos bin Said ruled from 1970 until his death in 2020 and presided over a period of rapid modernization known as the Omani Renaissance. Oman is a member of the [[United Nations|United Nations]], the [[Arab League|Arab League]] and the [[Non-Aligned Movement|Non-Aligned Movement]].

Persian polymath known for mathematics, astronomy, philosophy and poetry. Born in Nishapur, in the [[Seljuk Empire|Seljuk Empire]], Khayyam was the first to provide a general solution of all [[Cubic equation|third-degree polynomials]], using the intersection of two [[Conic section|conic sections]]. He also contributed to understanding [[Euclid|Euclid]]'s parallel axiom, and the Saccheri quadrilateral is sometimes called the Khayyam–Saccheri quadrilateral. As an astronomer he directed the observatory at [[Isfahan|Isfahan]], where he designed the Jalali calendar, a solar calendar with a 33-year intercalation cycle that provided the basis for the Persian calendar still in use. He spent time at [[Samarkand|Samarkand]] early in his career. His quatrains, the *Rubaiyat*, became widely known through Edward FitzGerald's 1859 English translation.

Egyptian actor, generally regarded as the greatest male film star of Egypt. Sharif began his career in Egypt in the early 1950s and became internationally known for *Lawrence of Arabia* (1962), in which he played Sherif Ali opposite [[Peter O'Toole|Peter O'Toole]] and earned an Academy Award nomination. He won a Golden Globe Award for *Doctor Zhivago* (1965). His career encompassed more than 100 films. A lifelong [[Horse racing|horse racing]] enthusiast, he once ranked among the world's top [[Contract bridge|contract bridge]] players. He was one of only 25 recipients of [[UNESCO|UNESCO]]'s Sergei Eisenstein Medal.

French actor. Sy was initially best known in France for comedy sketches with Fred Testot on the Canal+ show *Service après-vente des émissions* (2005–2012). He gained international recognition in *The Intouchables* (2011), a comedy-drama for which he won the César Award for Best Actor, becoming the first Black recipient of the award. Later films include *X-Men: Days of Future Past* (2014), *Jurassic World* (2015) and *Chocolat* (2016). He also starred in the [[Netflix|Netflix]] series *Lupin*, from 2021.
